extracted.intended_audience: Viceroy of Peru, naval captains, pilots, sailors, and royal officials tasked with outfitting or supporting an imperial voyage (early 17th-century Spanish colonial administration)
extracted.subtask_description: Formal royal orders and captain's instructions governing the outfitting, staffing, discipline, religious observance, reporting, and succession arrangements for a maritime discovery expedition (Pedro Fernandez de Quiros, 1603–1605). Applies to Viceroys, Admirals, captains, and ship crews responsible for carrying out the voyage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of two very good ships
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘...you are to give him two very good ships with which he will be satisfied, to fit them out and provide them with the number of people necessary, well victualled, and supplied with munitions and arms requisite for so long a voyage.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ships must be sufficient for long ocean navigation, purchased or provided, fitted out with crew, provisions, munitions, artillery and clothing. The fleet in the narrative also included a small launch/zabra for rescue and auxiliary tasks. (Context: ships are to enable the Captain to accomplish the discovery.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and accounting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The cost of the preparations, of the people who will be embarked, of the provisions, munitions, clothing, and other things necessary for the voyage, is to be defrayed from my royal revenues...’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royal revenues are authorized to pay expedition expenses; designated officials/accountants are ordered to receive and pass expenditures with the Viceroy’s letters of payment without seeking other authority. This establishes approved fiscal procedure and exempts local officers from seeking further authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of barter goods for natives
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The ships are also to be supplied with things for bartering with natives, if they should reach places where this can be done, in conformity with the general orders which you and your predecessors have for similar discoveries...’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voyage provisioning must include trade goods appropriate for exchange with indigenous peoples, and these must conform to existing general orders for discoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of missionaries and medical staff
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘You are to give orders that some bare-foot friars, of the Order of St. Francis, exemplary and of good life, are taken...’ and the narrative notes 'the said six friars of the Order of St. Francis, also four brothers of Juan de Dios to cure the sick.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedition should carry clergy (for conversion and spiritual needs) and medical caregivers; persons chosen should be exemplary and suited to the mission of conversion and care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obedience to the appointed Captain
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘...ordering them to obey and respect the said Captain during the voyage out and home, as their leader and superior, whom I name for that position from this time, obeying him in all things.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appointed Captain represents royal authority aboard and must be obeyed in all matters; obedience is a formal requirement backed by admonitions of discipline and possible sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt compliance with royal orders (no delays or impediments)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘I charge and order you very positively to comply promptly with my orders, without interposing doubts or difficulties...’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local authorities must not obstruct or delay the execution of the royal command even if the order did not pass through the usual channel (Council of the Indies); urgency and deference to the King's will are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt, protection and succour in ports
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘...you shall receive, protect, and succour the said Captain and his people in my ports and lands, and provide them with whatever is necessary to complete the said voyage without delay...’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any port or provincial authority is ordered to aid the Captain and crew on arrival: provide supplies, assistance, and refrain from imposing impediments; assistance is a duty tied to seeking royal approval/favour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting obligations to the Crown
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘By the first ship you are to report the arrival of the said Captain Quiros in those my kingdoms, and how you have furnished him with the said two ships, and provided him with all that is necessary...’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials must promptly inform the King (via first available ship) about arrival and compliance with provisioning and outfitting orders; the King expects news and will 'look out' anxiously for it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession provision in event of Captain's failure or death
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘...if he should fail through sickness, accident, or death... you shall nominate a person equally able and sufficient for the duty, in order that with the said despatches and papers and writings... such a person may continue the said discovery.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A contingency plan is required: local authorities must select a qualified successor able to continue the enterprise and provide that successor with necessary assistance and support as previously ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and credentials of the Captain/pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions praising Quiros: 'a great pilot with much experience of the South Sea ... expert in making globes, and charts for navigating; that he well understands the use of instruments necessary for navigation, and that he showed them two of his own invention...' and that he was 'a worker, quiet, disinterested, of decent life, zealous for the service of God and for my service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred captain/pilot qualities: extensive practical experience, proven discoveries (maps/writings), technical skill in chart/globe making and instrument use/innovation, good moral character, piety, and loyalty to the Crown and God. Endorsements by learned authorities (mathematicians, geographers) strengthen suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed accounts and observations to be delivered
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘...to deliver and account to me of what he had seen and discovered, and of the observations he will have made by land and sea during his navigation, in conformity with the orders he has received.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Captain must prepare despatches, maps, and memorials documenting discoveries, peoples, resources, needle variation observations, latitudes/longitudes, and any other navigational or ethnographic information required by the Crown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Christian, political, and military discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘I specially charge the said Admiral that he is to maintain Christian, political, and military discipline among the men of his ship.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders must enforce a strict code combining religious observance, political loyalty (to the Crown), and military order among crew and soldiers; discipline is both moral and hierarchical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of blasphemy and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘...he is to see that they do not curse nor blaspheme... the person so offending forfeiting his ration for that day... if he repents... pardoned the first time, but for the second, third, or other times he may be put in irons, or fined for the benefit of souls in purgatory; and this may not be remitted. And that this may be known to all, a copy of this chapter is to be nailed to the ship’s main mast.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blasphemy is explicitly outlawed aboard; prescribed punishments range from ration forfeiture to irons and fines for repeated offences; public posting of the rule is required to ensure crew awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of gambling (dice/cards) and removal of gaming instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘...not to consent to any playings with dice or cards... if by chance there should be any playing cards found in his ship, or dice (except for playing at backgammon), he is to throw them overboard... and if the games at tables cause disputes and trouble, they are also to be thrown overboard...’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gambling is banned (with specific exception of backgammon); gaming devices are to be destroyed overboard; gambling that provokes disputes is to be suppressed to avoid mischief and disorder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily communal religious observance
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘He is to take great care that every day, in the afternoon, all the people go on their knees before an altar where there are images of Christ and of the Virgin Mary, and that the Litany of Our Lady of Loreto is recited...’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory daily devotional practice is required for all aboard (afternoon prayers, recitation of specified litanies) to solicit divine guidance and protection for the voyage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent disrespect to the royal person and punish accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Further, he is to be very vigilant in preventing free or disrespectful words being spoken of the royal person or his service: and those who so offend are to be punished promptly and with rigour...’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speech or conduct disrespectful of the King or his service is a punishable offence; commanders must be vigilant and apply rigorous sanctions to preserve loyalty and political order aboard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commanders must treat crew kindly and maintain officers' authority
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Further, he is to take care and use much diligence in treating kindly and lovingly all the people under his charge, and to honour and maintain each one of his officers in the posts they occupy, and to cause them to be respected and to respect each other.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While enforcing discipline, commanders are required to exercise humane leadership: treat crew kindly, support officers in their posts, and foster mutual respect to preserve cohesion and morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisioning for colonization/settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative inventory: 'provisions of all kinds for one year, iron implements, fruits and animals of Peru for those who should form a settlement...' and small pieces of artillery, arquebuses and muskets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the expedition contemplates establishing a settlement, it must carry tools, foodstuffs, livestock/plant stock, and defensive armaments suitable for sustaining settlers for an extended initial period (example given: one year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and development of navigational instruments and observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quiros offered instruments 'one by which to know, in navigating, the difference made by the needle between the N.E. and N.W. points, and the other for taking an altitude with more ease and accuracy... they concluded... there could not fail to be either a continental land or a number of islands...' and he proposed to 'make quite clear the true differences made by the needle in variation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expeditions should employ tested instruments and observational techniques to solve navigational uncertainties (magnetic variation, latitude/longitude) and produce accurate charts; innovation in instruments is commended and may be supported by learned endorsements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance pay and security for crew wages
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion: 'it was represented that the pay should be in advance, and the persons who raised the question claimed that it should be given on board the ships, or with good securities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crew wages should be advanced with appropriate securities (possibly paid aboard or guaranteed) to ensure commitment and prevent disputes about compensation during long voyages.
